boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Galveston record (January 1, 1863) in Operations Against Galveston [December 1862-January 1863]. Magruder's preparations from November 1862, the Cambria episode of January 3 and the later blockade are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names Companies D, G and I of the 42nd Massachusetts and the blockading ships, and four Confederate gunboats with district troops, without figures; the live field reads 0. Davis says the shore enemy was not less than 3,000 with some twenty guns, and, by their own account, as many on the gunboats. Magruder says he called for 300 volunteers for the boats, gave Cook a storming party of about 500, and had six siege pieces, a railroad-mounted 8-inch gun and fourteen field pieces; he lists the Union vessels and their guns and says the Union land force's strength was unknown to him.
claims.rationale: Opponents' estimates and partial Confederate details: Davis's 3,000 is his January 1 estimate of the shore force; Magruder's call for 300 volunteers preceded the attack, and the 500-man storming party and the guns are his January 1 dispositions. No return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Magruder says the Union land force was at the end of a long wharf under the ships' guns, behind two lines of barricades with portions of the wharf removed, so the storming party had to wade; the water was deep and the ladders too short. Davis says they had barricaded the wharf in two places and the building inside. Magruder says Fort Point was open in the rear.
claims.rationale: The wharf position was prepared by the Union troops; tag unresolved. No map verification (Long's map not inspected).

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Major General John B. Magruder, Colonel Isaac S. Burrell and Commander W. B. Renshaw (navy). Magruder led the center assault and fired the signal gun, and credits Leon Smith with the boats and Green with the troops on them. Davis says Burrell sent him to the gunboats to ask for the men to be taken off. Both say Renshaw was killed when the Westfield was blown up.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; Burrell and Renshaw left no inspected report. No automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and the live field read 650 (US 600; CS 50). Magruder gives about 600 prisoners on January 1, 350 exclusive of officers on January 2, and 300 or 400 in his February report; his own loss not over 25 killed and 50 wounded on January 2 and 26 killed and 117 wounded in February. Davis thinks not over 20 of his men were wounded and knows of none killed.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Prisoner counts include naval crews; the frozen 600 is not traced.

open_questions: Banks's, Burt's and Long's accounts (read, not selected), the naval reports cited by the compiler (Annual Report of the Secretary of the Navy, 1863), Burrell's own account, returns and Long's map remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Davis's January 10, 1863 report and Magruder's January 1-3 and February 26, 1863 reports are interested accounts from opposite sides. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
